title: Sample a stored pool at random
statement: To estimate a single-try or best-of-several rate from a stored pool of scored candidates, sample the pool at random or generate afresh.
example: Read off the top of a score-sorted list, one model's single-try rate came out at 99.11%, which was its best-of-8 rate.
detail: In the AP work, each prompt's eight candidate scores were stored sorted best first, so the first entry, or the best of the first two, always returned the best-of-8 score (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/feedback_k8_bon_winner_trap_2026_05_11.md`). On one day that mistake was reported twice, as a single-try rate and as a best-of-2 rate, both 99.11%; a fresh single-try run that day scored 82.67% (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/FINAL_PLAN_2026_05_11_v3.md`). The rule since is to simulate a smaller pool by sampling stored candidates at random, or to generate afresh (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/feedback_k8_bon_winner_trap_2026_05_11.md`).

evidence.quote: True K=N from K=8 data requires random pair sampling.

The `all_scores` array is sorted DESCENDING by IB score (winner first). Slicing the first N entries gives you the TOP N from the K=8 pool, and the max of that is always `all_scores[0]` = the K=8 winner.
OR fresh K=N generation, which is rigorous but expensive.
On 2026-05-11, orch reported "B0161 K=2 BoN = 99.11% mean" computed from existing K=8 data via `max(all_scores[:2])`. This number is identical to K=8 winner pass rate.
K=1 was 99.11% per K=8 candidate-0 → wrong (sorted-by-score artifact).
**1h ago**: UPLIFT-1 single-seed K=1 T=0 = 82.67% on v43-soup `ty16vgj9`.
